high.title: Dollar-Won Pares Gains as Trump Prepares Final Decision on Iran Deal, Closes at 1,504.70 Won
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate declined in New York trading to close at 1,504.70 won, up only 1.90 won from Seoul's close but down 3.20 won from intraday highs around 1,507.90 won. The pullback occurred after President Trump announced he would make a final decision on an Iran war agreement MOU and lifted the naval blockade against Iran. This geopolitical development reduced safe-haven demand for the dollar. For KRW traders, this represents significant intraday volatility driven by geopolitical risk sentiment. The ability to hold below 1,505 levels suggests some stabilization, but ongoing Iran negotiations remain a key volatility driver. Watch for further developments in U.S.-Iran talks and any Federal Reserve commentary that could influence dollar direction.

high.title: Five Major Banks' Loan-Deposit Rate Spread Narrows to 1.388% After One Month
high.summary: South Korean banks' net interest margins showed the first contraction in a month, with the loan-deposit spread narrowing to 1.388% in April, down 0.124bp from March. This occurred as household deposit rates rose to 2.95% (+3.2bp) while loan rates fell to 4.26% (-4.2bp). The margin compression reflects both competitive pressure on deposit rates and potentially softer loan demand. For bond investors, rising deposit rates signal continued competition for funding and potential upward pressure on bank funding costs. This trend could pressure bank profitability if it continues, making bank bonds potentially less attractive. Monitor whether this represents a temporary adjustment or the start of a sustained margin compression cycle.

high.title: Shinhan Bank Sees Dollar-Won at 1,490-1,530 in June - 'Neither War Nor Peace, Status Quo Prevails'
high.summary: Shinhan Bank forecasts USD/KRW will trade in a 1,490-1,530 won range in June, expecting limited downside despite ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations. The bank cites difficulty reaching substantive agreements and potential market overreaction ahead of new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting as key risks. They note the provisional ceasefire extension and nuclear negotiations remain fragile due to disagreements over Strait of Hormuz passage rights. For FX traders, this suggests a rangebound market with 1,490 as key support and 1,530 as resistance. The wide 40-won range reflects high uncertainty around geopolitical outcomes and new Fed leadership. Position sizing should account for elevated volatility around these events.

medium.title: Busan Bank Sees Dollar-Won at 1,460-1,530 in June - Foreign Capital Flows to Determine Direction
medium.summary: Busan Bank forecasts USD/KRW in 1,460-1,530 won range for June, identifying foreign capital flows as the key directional driver. The bank notes upward pressure from delayed U.S.-Iran talks, reduced Fed cut expectations, and continued foreign stock selling, while seeing downward factors accumulating. This wider range suggests greater uncertainty than Shinhan Bank's forecast.

medium.title: NDF at 1,506.30/1,506.70 Won - Down 0.35 Won
medium.summary: The one-month USD/KRW NDF declined 0.35 won to 1,506.50 won (mid) in New York trading overnight. The dollar weakened after Trump mentioned making a "final decision" on Iran peace talks. NDF positioning suggests modest dollar weakness expectations near-term.

medium.title: San Francisco Fed President Says Monetary Policy Stance Appropriate, Opposes Harmful Tightening
medium.summary: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly stated current monetary policy is appropriately positioned and emphasized avoiding harmful tightening while restoring price stability. Her dovish stance contrasts with hawkish sentiment elsewhere and could influence dollar direction if it signals broader Fed thinking.

medium.title: Philadelphia Fed President Says Monetary Policy 'Moderately Restrictive, in Appropriate Position'
medium.summary: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson described current policy as "moderately restrictive" and appropriately positioned to combat high inflation. She noted inflation was elevated before Iran tensions and attributed it to multiple shocks rather than structural changes, with long-term expectations remaining stable.
